issues.description: The template's Bitmap24 header declares a method named write(const std::string&), but the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines save(const std::string&). The rest of the code (main.cpp) and the solution repository use bitmap.save(...). This name/signature mismatch between the header and the implementation will prevent successful compilation and is likely to confuse students about which API to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the header and implementation agree on the method name. Either change example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to declare void save(const std::string& i_filename); (recommended, to match the implementation and usage in main.cpp), or rename/implement Bitmap24::write(...) in Bitmap24.cpp and update usages. Ensure the template header matches the solution's API (save) to avoid compilation/link errors.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 class method name is inconsistent in the template: the header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) declares a method named 'write', but the implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) and usage in main (example_program/src/main.cpp) use 'save'. The solution repository consistently uses 'save'. This mismatch will confuse students about which API to implement and will cause compilation errors (member not declared) or require unnecessary renaming work.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template to use the same identifier as the implementation and usage. Rename the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'write(const std::string &i_filename)' to 'save(const std::string &i_filename)', matching example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp and main.cpp (and the solution). Alternatively, rename the implementation to 'write' and update main.cpp accordingly, but prefer changing the header to 'save' to match the solution.
